subject: Speeding up runif() in a for() loop.

messages.author: 6e9330056c1883ae
messages.subject: Speeding up runif() in a for() loop.
parts:
Hi all,

I'm running large monte carlo simulation over a grid of data and I have a bottle neck with a subroutine. I hoping perhaps there is a way use apply() to speed this up, but I've been unable to come up with anything yet.

In my simulation I'm trying to estimate an upper and lower bound for the chemical weathering flux (cflux) at each grid cell.

In a general sense, chemical weathering flux is calculated by multiplying denudation (denud) by a chemical depletion factor (cdf) - so:

cflux  = denud * cdf

In reality, for a given denud value, there is an interval of plausible cdf values that I want to sample from.

I apologize in advance for the poor quality of the code and comments that follow.

-- code follows -- 
#I simulate a set of denudation values for a single grid cell via another 
#subroutine import them as the vector v.denud.
#Since I'm not including the other subroutine - I'll just generate some data.

n <- 100
v.denud <- round(runif ( n, 1, 100 ))

#For each denudation value there is a plausible range of CDF values.
#This range (q.025 - q.975) of values is held in d.cdf.
#Again - just generate some data.

denud <- seq ( 1, 100, 1 )
q.025 <- runif ( n, 0, 0.5 )
q.975 <- runif ( n, 0.5, 1 )
d.cdf <- as.data.frame ( cbind ( denud, q.025, q.975 ) )

#clean up unneeded objects
rm ( denud, q.025, q.975)


#For each element in v.denud I sample over the interval in d.cdf where v.denud[i] == d.cdf$denud.
#First, I preallocate a output v.cdf
v.cdf <- rep ( NA, n )

#Use a for loop to cycle through each element in the vector v.denud
for ( i in 1 :  length(v.denud) ) {
 
  #extract the lower end of the sampling interval for the ith element in v.denud
  lower <- d.cdf$q.025 [ which ( d.cdf$denud == v.denud[i]  ) ]
 
  #extract the upper end of the sampling interval in v.denud
  upper <- d.cdf$q.975[ which ( d.cdf$denud == v.denud[i] ) ]

  #Finally, simulate a single CDF value for the ith element in v.denud
  v.cdf[i] <- runif ( 1, lower, upper)
}

#Multiply Denudation by CDF to estimate chemical weathering flux
v.cflux <- v.denud * v.cdf

#extract quantiles for chemical weathering flux
quantile ( v.cflux, probs = c( 0.025, 0.50, 0.975 ) )


-- end code --

In my real code, the for() loop iterates over a vector of length 10000 which takes a few seconds to run. That speed is unacceptable given the grid sizes that I'm running this over. Is there anyway to speed this up? 

Thanks!

-s

--
Scott Morford
PhD Candidate - Soil and Biogeochemistry
University of California Davis
http://houlton.lawr.ucdavis.edu/

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Speeding up runif() in a for() loop.
parts:
Does this do what you want?

It samples n uniform random numbers. The lower bound for element i is the ith element of q.025 and the upper bound for it is the ith element of q.975.

q.025 <- runif ( n, 0, 0.5 )
q.975 <- runif ( n, 0.5, 1 )

runif(n = n, min = q.025, max = q.975)

Dave

messages.author: b35e99045f6c74c2
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Speeding up runif() in a for() loop.
parts:
Hi Scott,

I'm not quite sure what you're doing, so I apologize if I've misunderstood. But it seems like you have two data sources: a vector v.denud of values, and you wish to find the value of v.denud in d.cdf$denud, then grab that corresponding row's min and max to draw a uniform sample from, parameterized by these values.

If this is the case, you can do a single initial match(), and then use runif (which takes vectorized arguments) in one go, without any for loops for apply(). However, match() with return NA if it can't match, and it only grabs the first entry — your data must be "joinable" for it to work correctly. Here is an illustration: 

 > match(c(10, 1), c(10, 10))
1 NA
> match(c(10, 1), c(0, 0))
NA NA

The for loop is slow here because it's doing a O(n) calculation every time you enter d.cdf$denud == v.denud[i]. This just means that for your n elements, the runtime complexity is limiting in n (in contrast to a constant, or n^2, etc). In fact, even just refactoring this so it's done once in a loop rather than twice (and removing unnecessary which statements — `[` knows how to handle vectors of logicals) drops the runtime from 20 seconds to 17 (repeated N=1e4 times).

So if I understand you correctly (and again, not sure I see the big picture of your problem), you could do something like:

v.denud.alt <- round(runif(n, 1, 100))
matchApproach <- function() {
  idx <- match(v.denud.alt, d.cdf$denud)
  lower <- d.cdf$q.025[idx]
  upper <- d.cdf$q.975[idx]
  return(runif(length(idx), lower, upper))
}

This runs in 0.8 seconds (repeated N=1e4 times) to the for loop's 20 seconds (via system.time()). I've set the seed before each approach and the results are consistent. 

Vince

Hi Dave,

In the code you present above, it appears that you are randomly
(uniformly) sampling from a set of uniform random intervals. If I am
understanding this correctly, this is not what I'm looking for.

Although in the code I present I generate random intervals for each
denud value in d.cdf, the d.cdf data.frame is in reality a set of
empirical intervals that I import from a table.

I generated d.cdf on the fly to ease running of the code - I should have
been more clear - sorry.

So say, for a denud value of 100 I know that q.025 = 0.2 and q.975 = 0.5.

For a denud value of 20 I know that q.025 = 0.4 and q.975 = .80. etc...

Essentially, the cdf interval does not change for a given denud value.

I am trying to extract the correct cdf sampling interval based upon the
denud value in v.denud and then produce a single uniform random sample
of cdf for each v.denud element.

clear as mud?

-S

>>> v.denud <- round(runif ( n, 1, 100 ))
>>>
>>> #For each denudation value there is a plausible range
>>> #of CDF values.This range (q.025 - q.975) of values is
>>> #held in d.cdf. Again - just generate some data.
>>>
>>>
>>> denud <- seq ( 1, 100, 1 )
>>> q.025 <- runif ( n, 0, 0.5 )
>>> q.975 <- runif ( n, 0.5, 1 )
>>> d.cdf <- as.data.frame ( cbind ( denud, q.025, q.975 ) )
>>>
>>> #clean up unneeded objects
>>>
>>> rm ( denud, q.025, q.975)
>>>
>>> #For each element in v.denud I sample over the interval
>>> #in d.cdf where v.denud[i] == d.cdf$denud.
>>> #First, I preallocate a output v.cdf.
>>>
>>>
>>> v.cdf <- rep ( NA, n )
>>>
>>> #Use a for loop to cycle through each element in the
>>> #vector v.denud
>>>
>>>
>>> for ( i in 1 : length(v.denud) ) {
>>>
>>> #extract the lower end of the sampling interval for the
>>> #ith element in v.denud.
>>>
>>>
>>> lower <- d.cdf$q.025 [ which ( d.cdf$denud == v.denud[i] ) ]
>>>
>>> #extract the upper end of the sampling interval in v.denud
>>> upper <- d.cdf$q.975[ which ( d.cdf$denud == v.denud[i] ) ]
>>>
>>> #Finally, simulate a single CDF value for the ith
>>> #element in v.denud
>>>
>>>
>>> v.cdf[i] <- runif ( 1, lower, upper)
>>>
>>> }
>>>
>>> #Multiply Denudation by CDF to estimate chemical weathering flux
>>> v.cflux <- v.denud * v.cdf
>>>
>>> #extract quantiles for chemical weathering flux

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Speeding up runif() in a for() loop.
parts:
I just wanted to let everyone know that Vince's solution worked perfectly.

I was able to replace my loop:
for ( i in 1 : length(v.denud) ) {

....
}

with:

idx <- match(v.denud, d.cdf$denud)

lower <- d.cdf$q.025[idx]
upper <- d.cdf$q.975[idx]

v.cdf <- (runif(length(idx), lower, upper))

Thanks again to Vince, Dave, and Mason for their input!

-S

On Wed, Feb 6, 2013 at 11:36 AM, Scott Morford <slmo...@ucdavis.edu> wrote:
> Hi Vince,
>

> you've suggested a little bit and get back to the list with my progress.
> Thank you everyone!

> On 2/6/2013 11:16 AM, Vince S. Buffalo wrote:
>>
>> Oh, and I forgot to mention: matchApproach()was my dummy function for
>> testing speeds; ignore it and wrap it in your own meaningful function if
>> you use that code.
>>
>> Vince
>>
>>
>> On Wed, Feb 6, 2013 at 11:14 AM, Vince S. Buffalo
>> <vsbu...@gmail.com>wrote:
>>
>>> Hi Scott,
>>>
>>> I'm not quite sure what you're doing, so I apologize if I've
>>> misunderstood. But it seems like you have two data sources: a vector
>>> v.denud of values, and you wish to find the value of v.denud in
>>> d.cdf$denud, then grab that corresponding row's min and max to draw a
>>> uniform sample from, parameterized by these values.
>>>
>>> If this is the case, you can do a single initial match(), and then use
>>> runif (which takes vectorized arguments) in one go, without any for loops
>>> for apply(). However, match() with return NA if it can't match, and it
>>> only grabs the first entry — your data must be "joinable" for it to work

>>> correctly. Here is an illustration:
>>>
>>> > match(c(10, 1), c(10, 10))
>>> 1 NA
>>>>
>>>> match(c(10, 1), c(0, 0))
>>>
>>> NA NA
>>>
>>> The for loop is slow here because it's doing a O(n) calculation every
>>> time
>>> you enter d.cdf$denud == v.denud[i]. This just means that for your n
>>> elements, the runtime complexity is limiting in n (in contrast to a
>>> constant, or n^2, etc). In fact, even just refactoring this so it's done
>>> once in a loop rather than twice (and removing unnecessary which
>>> statements
>>> — `[` knows how to handle vectors of logicals) drops the runtime from 20

>>> seconds to 17 (repeated N=1e4 times).
>>>
>>> So if I understand you correctly (and again, not sure I see the big
>>> picture of your problem), you could do something like:
>>>
>>> v.denud.alt <- round(runif(n, 1, 100))
>>> matchApproach <- function() {
>>> idx <- match(v.denud.alt, d.cdf$denud)
>>> lower <- d.cdf$q.025[idx]
>>> upper <- d.cdf$q.975[idx]
>>> return(runif(length(idx), lower, upper))
>>> }
>>>
>>> This runs in 0.8 seconds (repeated N=1e4 times) to the for loop's 20
>>> seconds (via system.time()). I've set the seed before each approach and
>>> the results are consistent.
>>>
>>> Vince
>>>
>>>
